title: The Inheritance of Ashcombe
premise: When the coffin of Ashcombe's revered founder, Edmund Vane, is exhumed for a tercentenary reinterment and found empty, cathedral archivist Gideon Halloran is pulled into a mystery the town has spent three centuries burying. Following ledgers, smugglers' tides, and a forbidden romance in Vane's own letters, Gideon discovers the founder never died at Ashcombe at all—he fled with another man's wife, and the town's founding wealth was built on silencing them. As Gideon closes the case, they must choose between exposing the lie that sustains Ashcombe's powerful families and protecting the descendant who helped them find the truth; the novel ends with the tide giving up its secret—a second skeleton beneath the harbor stones—and Gideon choosing truth over invisibility, resigning their post as the crypt is finally unlocked.
about_author: Silas Nakamura is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing coastal church archives before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about small towns that keep their histories under lock and key.

chapters.title: The Tercentenary
chapters.summary: Gideon Halloran, POV. Preparations for exhuming founder Edmund Vane proceed despite Gideon's unease about disturbing the sealed crypt. Establishes Gideon's pride in closed cases and their careful invisibility within cathedral hierarchy. Emotional beat: quiet dread masked as professional routine.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The coffin is opened before the town and holds only river stones wrapped in 1720s linen. The crowd's reverence curdles into fear. Mayor Aldous Crane quietly asks Gideon to 'manage' the finding. Emotional beat: shock hardening into resolve—this case will be closed properly.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. In the archive, Gideon finds burial expenses recorded twice for Vane and a page razored from the interment register. First appearance of Wren Calloway, a marine archaeologist whose grandmother once worked the crypt. Emotional beat: the thrill of a thread to pull.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren shows Gideon harbor survey maps marking an anomaly beneath the old quay stones. She believes something was sunk there deliberately. Gideon resists partnership; duty says report, instinct says dig. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming over shared stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Crane Version
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Aldous Crane offers Gideon funding and promotion if the empty coffin is blamed on Victorian grave-robbers. Gideon notes the Cranes' name appears on every land deed after 1724. Emotional beat: first taste of how power leans on the archive.

chapters.title: Letters in a False Back
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Behind the archive's false panel, Gideon finds Vane's private correspondence—tender letters signed 'E.V.' to someone called only 'M,' full of flight plans and guilt. Emotional beat: falling into the past, recognizing love that defied duty as a mirror of their own guarded life.

chapters.title: M Is for Marlowe
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Wren identifies M: Mercy Marlowe, wife of Vane's business partner Josiah, who vanished the same winter Vane supposedly died. Town legend calls her a witch. Wren's own family lore ties her ancestors to Mercy's household. Emotional beat: history becoming personal.

chapters.title: Closed for Good
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon interviews the last living elder of the Vane trust, Dame Iris Vane, who warns: 'That case was closed so it could stay closed.' That night the archive is broken into; the letters are gone. Emotional beat: violation, and the realization staying invisible failed.

chapters.title: Suspects in Silk
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon catalogs who benefits from the lie: the Crane family trust, the cathedral dean, the heritage board. A threatening note arrives quoting Gideon's own archival shorthand—someone inside knows their methods. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening focus.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. At spring low tide, Wren and Gideon dive the quay anomaly and find a lead-lined chest: Mercy Marlowe's belongings, including a locket with two portraits and a confession written in Vane's hand. Emotional beat: awe and terror—the case is no longer paper.

chapters.title: The Confession
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The document reveals Vane staged his death to flee with Mercy; Josiah pursued them, and only one of the three came back. The bones beneath the quay belong to either Vane or Josiah. Emotional beat: grief for lovers destroyed by the town they founded.

chapters.title: Dean's Gambit
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The dean suspends Gideon, citing 'unauthorized handling of relics,' and seals the crypt with a new lock. Aldous privately threatens Wren's excavation permits. Emotional beat: isolation—the cost of refusing to look away.

chapters.title: Dame Iris Breaks
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Dame Iris, dying and unafraid now, confesses her family has guarded the secret for generations: Josiah returned alone, blackmailed the town, and his descendants became the Cranes. Emotional beat: pity replacing suspicion; the weight of inherited silence.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Cross-referencing tide tables and Josiah's 'burial' record, Gideon proves Josiah's coffin is also empty—and that the body under the quay must be Vane, killed trying to escape with Mercy. Emotional beat: the case snapping shut intellectually before it can close legally.

chapters.title: Fire in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Arson guts the archive wing; Gideon barely escapes with the confession and locket. The dean blames Gideon's 'carelessness.' Emotional beat: rage and loss—everything Gideon built burning around them.

chapters.title: Ally Among Ashes
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Junior verger Tamsin admits she copied the razored register page years ago and produces it: Josiah signed as witness to a burial that never happened. Other townsfolk begin coming forward, tired of the lie. Emotional beat: solidarity rising from ruin.

chapters.title: Crane Unbound
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. Aldous, cornered by the evidence, offers Gideon everything—reinstatement, silence, Wren's permits—in exchange for the confession. He reveals he knew about the quay anomaly all along. Emotional beat: temptation offered plainly, and refused.

chapters.title: The Unlocked Crypt
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon uses their archivist's authority one last time to open the sealed crypt publicly, presenting the chain of documents before the whole town. The dean collapses; Aldous walks out. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken aloud where silence was law.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Wren, POV. The quay stones are lifted. Two skeletons, not one: Vane and, beside him, a woman's remains—Mercy never left him. They were killed together. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; the lovers reunited in death.

chapters.title: Reinterment
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. The town buries Vane and Mercy together, rewriting the founders' story. Dame Iris attends in a wheelchair; the Cranes do not. Gideon declines reinstatement. Emotional beat: mourning turned into ceremony, identity chosen over invisibility.

chapters.title: The Open Case
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon resigns, leaving the archive to Tamsin, and takes the one file they never closed—their own—as a gift to themselves. Final scene: Gideon and Wren walking the tideline at dawn. Emotional beat: peace earned, love allowed.

chapters.title: Ashcombe, After
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. One year later: the crypt is a public exhibit, the true history taught in schools, and a letter arrives from a Crane descendant asking, at last, to know the truth. Tamsin unlocks the door. Emotional beat: legacy transformed—secrets ending where curiosity begins.
